sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Collier County, FL?
sections.html:
The Collier County Tax Collector sends the bills and takes payment, the Property Appraiser sets values and decides exemptions, and the Clerk of the Circuit Court handles value appeals and tax deed sales. Each office answers a different question, so a call to the wrong one costs time.

The tax collector's mailing address is 3291 Tamiami Trail East, Naples, FL 34112. Property tax questions go to propertytax@colliertax.com or 239-252-8171. The Property Appraiser can be reached at (239) 252-8141 for value and exemption questions.

sections.h2: When is Collier County property tax due and what are the discounts?
sections.html:
Bills are payable in November, and paying early earns a discount that shrinks each month. The tax collector's page lists 4% for November, 3% for December, 2% for January and 1% for February, with the gross amount due in March and delinquency in April.

Collier County payment months, as printed by the tax collector
Month paidDiscount
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchGross amount due
AprilDelinquent

The collector does not accept post-dated checks. Florida's revenue department adds that unpaid taxes turn delinquent on April 1 and tax certificates are sold on unpaid items by June 1. All offices close on listed holidays, including Veterans Day, Thanksgiving and the day after, and on one training day in October.

sections.h2: How does the Collier County assessment and notice cycle work?
sections.html:
The Property Appraiser values property as of January 1 each year. In mid-August the appraiser mails a Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, often called the TRIM notice.

  • August: TRIM notice arrives, listing proposed values and tax.
  • September and October: local taxing authorities hold budget hearings.
  • November: the tax collector sends bills.

Non-homestead assessed value can rise no more than 10 percent a year under the state's limit. Read the TRIM notice closely, because it is the notice that starts the appeal clock.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Collier County property value?
sections.html:
File a petition with the Value Adjustment Board, whose clerk is the Collier Clerk of the Circuit Court. An assessment appeal is due within 25 days after the appraiser mails the TRIM notice, and the 2026 petition deadline of September 11 has passed.

Other petitions run on different clocks. The clerk's table lists these:

  • Exemption or classification denial: 30 days after the appraiser mails the denial, with all denials mailed by July 1
  • Tax deferral denial: 30 days after the tax collector mails the denial
  • Portability and change of ownership or control: 25 days after the TRIM notice

The filing fee is $50.00 per petition per parcel for most types and $15.00 for a portability petition. The board has two county commissioners, one school board member and two citizen members, and special magistrates hear the cases and recommend decisions. Late filing needs a good cause statement.

sections.h2: How should I read a Collier County tax bill?
sections.html:
The tax collector bills ad valorem tax, which means tax according to worth, on real estate and on a business's tangible personal property. A mill is $1 of tax per $1,000 of taxable value, and each taxing authority sets its own rate, so the county, school district, city and special districts all appear on one bill.

Three checks help before you pay or sell:

  • Match the parcel number and legal owner on the bill to your deed.
  • Confirm the homestead exemption shows on the bill if you applied by March 1.
  • Ask the tax collector whether any non-ad valorem charge is on the bill, because those are assessments rather than value-based tax.

The tax collector's site links to a tax search where you can pull a notice or receipt, and a mortgage lender that pays from escrow should still be checked against that record.

sections.h2: What homestead and exemption rules matter for a Collier County owner?
sections.html:
Apply with the Property Appraiser by March 1 of the tax year, and make the home your permanent residence by January 1. The exemption is up to $50,000, with the first $25,000 applying to all taxes including school taxes and the second $25,000 applying to value over $50,000 for non-school taxes.

Save Our Homes limits yearly growth in assessed value to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change. The state's chart shows a 2.7% cap for 2026. A sale resets the property to just value the following January 1, so a buyer's bill can differ sharply from the seller's. Portability lets an owner carry savings to a new Florida homestead if it is established within three years of January 1 of the year the old homestead was given up.

Homestead ends if the home is rented or stops being the permanent residence. Owners 65 or older may qualify for added local exemptions, and disabled veterans have separate benefits, so ask the appraiser which apply.

sections.h2: Can I delay or spread out Collier County property tax?
sections.html:
Yes, through tax deferral and the installment program, both listed on the tax collector's property tax page. Deferral of homestead tax requires Form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31 after the assessment year and covers the part above 5 percent of household income.

A permanent resident 65 or older may defer the part above 3 percent. The installment plan under section 197.222 needs an application by May 1 of the assessment year. Ask the tax collector for current terms, because deferral accrues interest and a lien.

sections.h2: What happens to property tax when I sell a Collier County house?
sections.html:
Unpaid current-year tax is settled at closing, normally by the closing agent from the proceeds. Ask for a payoff from the tax collector for your closing date, and confirm earlier years show paid.

If taxes stay unpaid, the county sells a certificate. The holder can apply for a tax deed after two years from April 1 of the issue year, and the clerk then runs the auction. Homestead property carries an opening bid that includes half of the latest assessed value. At the clerk's tax deed auction, a winning bidder pays within 24 hours, so a delinquent house can be lost quickly. For recording costs on your own sale, see the Collier County property records guide.

sections.h2: Where do I find Collier County tax deed and foreclosure listings?
sections.html:
The Collier Clerk posts both a tax deeds list and a foreclosure sale list on its records search page. The tax deeds list covers properties where the tax collector sold certificates for delinquent real estate taxes.

State law lets the tax collector award each certificate to the bidder who accepts the lowest interest rate, in quarter-percent steps, and unsold certificates go to the county at the maximum rate. The certificate holder may not contact the owner for payment until two years after April 1 of the issue year. A homeowner with a small delinquency has options before that point, since payment to the tax collector redeems the certificate, so ask the collector's office for a payoff early rather than waiting for a sale notice.

faqs.q: When does Collier County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: Delinquency starts in April, and the state date is April 1. The gross amount is due in March, with discounts only from November through February.

faqs.q: What early-payment discounts does Collier County offer?
faqs.a: The tax collector lists 4% for November, 3% for December, 2% for January and 1% for February. March is the gross amount.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Collier County assessment?
faqs.a: Petitions are due within 25 days after the appraiser mails the TRIM notice. The 2026 deadline was September 11, and most petitions carry a $50.00 filing fee.

faqs.q: Does Collier County accept post-dated checks for property tax?
faqs.a: No. The tax collector states that post-dated checks are not accepted for property tax bills.

faqs.q: Where do I send a Collier County property tax payment by mail?
faqs.a: Mail it to the Collier County Tax Collector, 3291 Tamiami Trail East, Naples, FL 34112. Questions go to 239-252-8171.
